title: Machine-Checked Christofides 3/2-Approximation and Polyhedral Complexity Barriers for the Traveling Salesperson Problem in Lean 4
abstract: This formalization develops a machine-checked theory of the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) on finite undirected graphs over Fin n in Lean 4 across two principal modules. First, in Christofides.lean (compared against ChallengeChristofides.lean), we formalize the complete Christofides-Serdyukov 3/2-approximation algorithm for Metric TSP: the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) lower bound (cost(T) <= OPT), Euler's handshaking parity invariant for odd-degree vertices, the minimum-weight perfect matching upper bound on odd-degree vertices (2 * cost(M) <= OPT) via alternating matching decomposition of shortcut cycles, multigraph degree parity of T U M, constructive existence of Eulerian circuits via Hierholzer cycle splicing and complete Christofides certificates, metric walk shortcutting contraction, and the unconditional 3/2-approximation guarantee in both exact integer scaling and real arithmetic. Second, in TSPComplexity.lean (compared against ChallengeTSPComplexity.lean), we formalize polyhedral and complexity-theoretic barriers for Decision TSP: a fuel-bounded branch-and-cut state machine with verified soundness, completeness, and support-pruned cycle-separation rank decision equivalence; the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson (DFJ) subtour cut inequality (every valid tour crosses any proper nonempty cut at least twice); the continuous Held-Karp LP relaxation embedding; a machine-checked proof that the 10-vertex Petersen graph fractional assignment (x_e = 2/3) strictly separates the Held-Karp relaxation from the integral TSP polytope with zero slack on singleton cuts and slack >= 2/3 on all nontrivial cuts; Yannakakis DFJ slack matrix nonnegativity and conditional Fiorini-Rothvoss PSD extension complexity scaling; and polynomial-time reductions from Hamiltonian Cycle and gadget-parameterized 3-SAT to Decision TSP.
